items.title: Nintendo Defends Decision to Cut Mario and Yoshi Easter Eggs From The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake
items.description: Nintendo has defended its decision to scrub the secret appearance of Mario characters from its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Nintendo has defended its decision to scrub the secret appearance of Mario characters from its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.

Hidden away inside Hyrule Castle, the game's original 1998 version included a wall of portraits that featured Mario, Luigi, Peach, Bowser, and Yoshi artwork taken from Super Mario 64.

Visit the same area in Nintendo's newly-launched Switch 2 version, however, and all references to the Mushroom Kingdom have been removed. On a similar note, a selection of Zelda: Twilight Princess artwork has also been cut, having been snuck in when Ocarina of Time was re-released on 3DS.

Now, Nintendo has addressed its choice to remove these Easter eggs — and said that what was once a more "carefree" approach within Nintendo to referencing other games has been reconsidered.

"Certainly, at the time, when we put those there, I don't think anybody thought it was too big a deal," legendary Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma told Game Informer. "Maybe there was a more carefree or comfortable approach to that sort of thing.

"But looking at it now... given the overall way that we're creating this world and giving the player that form of expression, if they look up and they think, 'Why is Yoshi there?' We don't want that moment to interrupt their experience of the world in that way. So we're feeling a little bit differently about it this time."

While some fans might feel like it's a shame to see this more carefree attitude to Easter eggs is gone, it's fair to point out that Mario 64 Easter eggs (or Skyward Sword ones, for that matter) would make less sense today. Mario 64 was launched on the same platform as Ocarina of Time, of course, while Skyward Sword was released contemporaneously with the game's 3DS port. (Maybe Switch 2 just needs a new Mario game to actually arrive?)

"I do remember at the time the designers on the 3DS version were really interested in placing Easter Eggs like that throughout the game," Aonuma continued, "and the timing of the release of Skyward Sword was such that it was perfect to go ahead and include that... [But] you don't want to interrupt the player's experience by seeing something that's unrelated to what they're currently doing in the game. So for that reason, we decided not to go that way."

"No hard feelings there," commented Skyward Sword director Hidemaro Fujibayashi, who returned as a producer for this remake.

And one Mario reference does still survive via Talon — a character who is an obvious nod to Mario with his bushy moustache, plus red and blue overalls. Check out his necklace, and you'll see his golden Bowser charm remains intact, all these years later.

Nintendo legend Shigeru Miyamoto has previously discussed the idea of the company's different franchises crossing over, and said that he wasn't a fan — except when it is Pikmin, which he wants to include wherever possible.

Earlier today, Nintendo revealed that Ocarina of Time had already shifted 5.2 million copies and become the Switch 2's fastest-selling game so far. Meanwhile, players have been having fun in-game by performing everything from Linkin Park to the Titanic theme on ocarina.

items.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Players Use In-Game Ocarina to Play Everything From Linkin Park, Titanic, and Japanese Supermarket Themes
items.description: The much anticipated remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launched on November 5, and one feature has fast become a big hit: the fact that you can now play any tune you like on Link’s ocarina. Now, social media has become awash with players sharing the results.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The much anticipated remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launched on November 5, and one feature has fast become a big hit: the fact that you can now play any tune you like on Link’s ocarina. Now, social media has become awash with players sharing the results.

People are tackling tunes from other video game series like Final Fantasy, anime such as Dragon Ball Z, and film scores including Titanic and The Lord of the Rings. Users often put a pun in the post, usually involving Link or Hyrule.

Over on X, @StevenxTCG got Link to play Linkin Park’s ‘In the End’ on the ocarina. The post proved unexpectedly popular, prompting him to follow up with a guide on how to play it yourself. On a more upbeat note, another poster responded with ‘Macarena of Time,’ their take on the '90s dance craze.

Okay, you guys wanted the notes so here they are. I also made a video so you can follow along lol

L - A - A - R - UP+L - UP+L - UP+L - UP+L - R



L - A - A - R - UP+L - UP+L - UP+L - UP+L - R

L - A - A - R - UP+L - UP+L - UP+L - UP+L - R - L (hold) https://t.co/BIY5vhPSPx

— Steven 💎 (@StevenxTCG) November 7, 2026

I see your Link-in Park and raise you Macarena of Time https://t.co/tOquHvAKFa

— chefspin (@chef_spin) November 8, 2026

Themes from other games also proved popular. @KOPPE_lunix posted their rendition of the emotional tearjerker ‘To Zanarkand’ from Final Fantasy 10 and also shared some guidance on how to play. Video game lecturer Dr. T. Wade Langer (aka ProfNoctis) posted a duet of Link and Cloud playing Final Fantasy 7’s main theme, adding that “I want music minigames in every game now.” Another popular choice was Kingdom Hearts’ Dearly Beloved.

時オカのオカリナで

♪ザナルカンドにて/ファイナルファンタジー10 https://t.co/5TEPMNHh1Q

— Koppe@いなかモン (@KOPPE_lunix) November 8, 2026

Main theme of FF7, as performed by my favorites. https://t.co/zel7RWX0cG

— ProfNoctis (@ProfNoctis) November 7, 2026

Link plays Dearly Beloved in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time ✨ https://t.co/CYM5kyG3N0

— KHWorld (@KHWorldWeb) November 7, 2026

More recent games also got some love, with players having a go at everything from Death Stranding’s BB’s theme to Kirby Air Riders’ main theme song Starlit Journey.

エアライダー https://t.co/0jfe0STvNI

— 五本木 葵 (@Gohongi_04) November 7, 2026

I played BB's theme from Death Stranding on the ocarina in Ocarina of Time

#OcarinaOfTime #DEATHSTRANDING https://t.co/UdVPNZThdd

— Jaymire (@set71374) November 8, 2026

Other users tried their hand at movie soundtracks. The main theme from Titanic was a popular choice, as were The Lord of The Rings movies. Naturally, Howard Shore’s ‘Concerning Hobbits’ from The Fellowship of the Ring became ‘Concerning Hylians.’

My Magnum Opus

Concerning Hylians https://t.co/h8V5Kpxkhv

— Il Seven lI (@MGylseth) November 7, 2026

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Titanic https://t.co/cji4tJti8q

— VideoArtGame (@VideoArtGame) November 7, 2026

Among Japanese players, store and supermarket jingles seem to be particularly popular, probably because their simple melodies are suited to the ocarina. One user tackled ‘Yobikomi-kun,’ a catchy ditty well-known to anyone who has spent time wandering supermarket aisles in Japan. Even discount store Don Quijote (where you can buy all manner of normal and bizarre things) got a rendition of its earworm jingle for the ‘Hyrule branch.’

呼び込みリンクくん

#NintendoSwitch2

#ゼルダの伝説 #時のオカリナ https://t.co/s2zHxJphHY

— あっちぇれらんど (@accelerando_xx) November 6, 2026

ドン・キホーテ　ハイラル店

#NintendoSwitch2

#ゼルダの伝説 #時のオカリナ https://t.co/VAs5MvOpTN

— 2KADA. (@_2KADA) November 8, 2026

Some users also tried playing Japan’s national anthem, prompting comments and jokes about how Link must be part of the Hojo samurai clan, because their crest closely resembles the triangles of the Triforce in Zelda.

生まれがどうにも怪しい時の勇者

#時のオカリナ https://t.co/M87OjkcsXh

— なぁーづる (@nazuru_1816wind) November 7, 2026

Perhaps predicting this trend, Nintendo also released an official Playable Ocarina. This physical replica of Link’s musical instrument comes with the added bonus that it can also be used with the game. If you play a melody towards the Switch 2’s microphone, Link in the game will play along with you.

Of course, playing songs on Link’s ocarina is also a game mechanic. By finding and learning songs, Link can do all manner of useful things like fast travel and solve puzzles. Check out our guide if you are struggling to find any of the 13 in-game songs.

Nintendo has announced Ocarina of Time has sold an impressive 5.2 million copies, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game after just four days on sale. items.title: PS5 Hits 100 Million Units Sold Mark 6 Years After Launch — Here's How It Compares to Other PlayStation Consoles
items.description: PlayStation 5 has shipped 100 million units, Sony has announced. Here's how it compares to the sales of other PlayStation consoles over the years.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
PlayStation 5 has shipped 100 million units, Sony has announced. The milestone comes ahead of the launch of GTA 6, which is expected to boost console sales significantly. It means PS5 has shipped an additional 2.1 million units in the 40 days since it last reported PS5 sales, at the end of September.

Sony Interactive Entertainment describes shipped units as “Cumulative Worldwide Hardware Unit Sales (Sell-in),” which isn’t sell-through to customers, but does give us an idea of how well the PS5 has sold.

PS5 hits 100 million six years after launch. The console released on November 12, 2020, in select countries and November 19, 2020, worldwide, amid the COVID pandemic and lockdowns. Console rival Microsoft launched the Xbox Series X and S at the same time, and does not report sales figures.

How does PS5 compare to other PlayStation consoles? It’s heading towards PS4’s 117 million total (as of June 30, 2022 — the latest data we have from Sony). It had already outsold the PS3’s 87.4 million total (as of March 31, 2017), and the PlayStation Portable’s 76.4 million as of March 31, 2012. It will soon overtake the original PlayStation’s 102.4 million, but is unlikely to surpass the PS2’s huge 160 million sales. Indeed, PS2 remains the best-selling console of all time, just ahead of the Nintendo Switch’s 157.2 million (as of September 30, 2026). Sony failed to disclose sales data for the PlayStation Vita, but it’s safe to say it wouldn’t have appeared high up on this list.

PlayStation hardware sales:

  • PlayStation 5: More than 100 million (As of November 10, 2026)
  • PlayStation 4: More than 117 million (As of June 30, 2022)
  • PlayStation 3: More than 87.4 million (As of March 31, 2017)
  • PSP (PlayStation Portable): More than 76.4 million (As of March 31, 2012)
  • PlayStation 2: More than 160 million (As of March 31, 2012)
  • PlayStation: More than 102.4 million (As of March 31, 2012)

Perhaps the more important question for Sony is how PS5 is selling launch-aligned versus the PS4. As it stands, the PS5 is around 5 million behind its predecessor, but it’s worth remembering that the market is in a very different place for PS5 at this point in its lifecycle than PS4 was. The main drag on PS5 — and indeed all console sales — is price rises due to the AI-fueled ‘RAMpocalypse.’ Traditionally, video game consoles get cheaper the older they get, which in turn boosts second half lifecycle sales. This generation has seen the opposite happen, with consoles getting more expensive and sales dropping off.

Still, Sony will be happy with how its gaming business is doing. Earlier this month, Sony raised its full-year forecast for PlayStation after higher net sales and operating income in the second quarter. And it has GTA 6 coming out next week.

It’s not all good news for PlayStation, however. With 2.4 million units sold, Marvel’s Wolverine is considered a disappointment. And just this week Sony continued its costly retreat from live service by canceling Haven’s Fairgames.

Thoughts naturally turn to the next-gen and the promise of PS6 and possibly even a PlayStation handheld. Reports indicate next-gen consoles could cost more than $1,000 at launch, so it’s hard to image what follows PS5 getting anywhere near the 100 million sold mark.

items.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a Huge Success for Nintendo — And Just Broke a Switch 2 Sales Record
items.description: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has broken a sale records for Nintendo, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game over its first four days of availability.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has broken sales records for Nintendo, and become the fastest-selling Switch 2 game over its first four days of availability.

Nintendo has already shifted 5.2 million copies of its newly-launched Zelda remake, the company announced today in a celebratory press release.

That means Zelda is selling faster than other notable Switch 2 arrivals such as Donkey Kong Bananza, Pokémon Pokopia and even Mario Kart World, which launched alongside the console last year. (Nintendo sold 3.5 million Switch 2 consoles over its first four days, with roughly 80% of those consoles sold in a bundle with Mario Kart World, at least in the U.S.)

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is Nintendo's big Switch 2 game for the holidays, so the firm will likely be pleased by its strong launch. It is one of the few other titles (hello, Barbie!) braving a November release, just a few weeks clear of this year (and decade)'s hugely-hyped arrival of Grand Theft Auto 6. But perhaps the firm has been wise to bet on Ocarina of Time's legendary status and broad audience being distinct enough to survive GTA's gravitational pull.

Originally released for the N64 back in 1998, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remains one of the highest-rated and most beloved games of all time. items.title: VisionQuest Post-Credits Scene Just Confirmed A Major Marvel Character Is Coming Back in Upcoming Avengers Films
items.description: The finale of VisionQuest confirmed that one of the most beloved characters from the MCU will be returning in the upcoming Avengers films, seemingly under the control of Doctor Doom.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Spoilers for VisionQuest and potentially Avengers: Doomsday are contained in the article below. You've been warned!

The finale of VisionQuest confirmed that one of the most beloved characters from the MCU will be returning in the upcoming Avengers films, seemingly under the control of Doctor Doom.

Following the conclusion of VisionQuest, Marvel snuck in a little teaser for Avengers: Doomsday and/or Secret Wars during the credits. The scene was excluded from advanced screeners provided to the press, so it came as a big surprise and shows that Marvel made a great deal of effort to keep this moment a secret.

The show cut back to the ending of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, where Wanda Maximoff, AKA Scarlet Witch, uses her powers to destroy the Darkhold and, in the process, sacrifices herself. items.title: Fortis Games Closes With Over 400 Jobs Impacted
items.description: Fortis Games, a studio behind mobile titles like Twilight Towers and Bloom & Breakfast, has closed its doors, impacting around 440 jobs.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Fortis Games, a studio behind mobile titles like Twilight Towers and Bloom & Breakfast, has closed its doors, impacting around 440 jobs.

CEO Steven Chiang confirmed the closure in a statement to GamesBeat on November 10, 2026. “Fortis has been a labor of love for so many of us and we’re disappointed we weren’t able to achieve the goals we set for ourselves when we started this journey more than five years ago,” he told the outlet.

“We have been fortunate to work with some of the most talented and dedicated people in this space. As we move forward, our primary focus will be on helping this talented team of individuals find new opportunities. Thank you to everyone who has supported us over the past five years. We are grateful for the collaboration and friendship we have shared with so many.”

Several former employees have spoken out about the closure in posts on LinkedIn. In one of these posts, game producer Gustavo Coronet confirmed that Las Vegas Sands Corp., Fortis Games’ parent company, chose to “end funding and part ways, terminating all of the contracts, worldwide.”

“Super proud of the work we’ve done. LVS’s decision does not delete the ground breaking and best-in class agentic development workflow the Octopus team has built, nor the massively solid soft launch metrics both our projects were achieving in such early stages of development,” he wrote.

In another post, former communications director Scott Butterworth suggested that Fortis’s “community-focused” approach to mobile games didn’t resonate enough with players to help it “get off the ground.”

“Ah, Fortis Games — what could have been. Despite our unique, community-focused approach to the mobile games market, we just couldn't seem to get off the ground, and today, we finally ran out of runway,” he wrote.

“The company has officially shuttered, abruptly putting more than 400 talented people out of work (myself included). Hilariously, I'm also in the process of relocating to Los Angeles, so hey, why not add a little more change on top, right?”

Fortis Gaming was founded in 2022 by Steven Chiang, former executive at Electronic Arts and Zynga. Based out of San Francisco, California, it was funded by Las Vegas Sands Corp. to help the casino brand expand outside of gambling. Fortis went on to acquire several games studios over the ensuing four years; on November 4, it announced that it was sunsetting Twilight Towers, a move that came a mere week before Fortis’s total closure.

This is the latest game studio to shut its doors after EA revealed that it had closed down BioWare, famous for AAA RPG series like Mass Effect and Dragon Age — a decision that has proven to be extremely unpopular among players, who are now campaigning for EA to do something, anything, with its IP to prevent them from languishing in obscurity.

items.title: Lanterns Season 2 in Doubt, Says DC Studios Insider
items.description: An insider at DC Studios suggests that HBO’s Lanterns is unlikely renewed for a second season in spite of rave reviews and audience interest, as told in a report from Variety.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
UPDATE: Variety has updated the wording of their initial report; previously, the outlet reported that an insider claimed Lanterns "didn't get renewed for a second season." Now, their report reads that the show "has yet to be renewed for a second season." Our article has been updated to reflect this change.

An insider at DC Studios suggests that HBO’s Lanterns is unlikely renewed for a second season in spite of rave reviews and audience interest, as told in a report from Variety.

Variety’s report comes on the heels of James Gunn and Peter Safran’s exit from DC Studios on Monday, November 9. In a statement to the public, Gunn cited a dislike for the more “corporate” aspect of his position, citing long hours that negatively impacted his personal relationships.

Unsurprisingly, fans are now worried about the future of the DCU, given that Gunn had only been in his role for four years with just three films to show for it. Superman was released to generally positive reception; Supergirl decidedly less so; Clayface was also a mixed bag, but Lanterns, the live-action show that released on HBO this year, was a massive success.

Boasting viewership numbers that rivaled the likes of The Pitt, it’s safe to say that audiences loved Kyle Chandler’s Hal Jordan and Aaron Pierre’s John Stewart, and hopes were high for a second season. In fact, it seemed almost inevitable — but, according to insiders, it didn’t quite “capture the zeitgeist.” Whatever that means.

(While Variety’s report initially claimed that Lanterns was not renewed for a second season, its newest update hints that a Season 2 is less likely due to this fact.) “People cannot wait to make another season of a hit show," the source said.

This news, if true, comes as quite a shock — but that seems to be the theme of the month, given Safran and Gunn’s unexpected exit. In October, series co-creator Damon Lindelof revealed that writers were already hashing out ideas for a second season, though it hadn’t been greenlit just yet.

Safran confirmed this news in an October interview with IGN, though he admitted that it hinged on whether or not the team could come up with a story worth following up from the first season.

"The episodic world is always going to be a really important part of our overall slate, it's a great way to tell stories that need more real estate than a feature film can offer you, and it's a great way to introduce characters that we then bring into the feature world," Safran told us. "And I think that Aaron Pierre and John Stewart are a perfect example of that. We introduced him in Lanterns, and audiences will see him next summer in Man of Tomorrow. So, it's really important to us in continuing to tell aspects of the story that we're not telling in the feature film world, so there's more to come.

"Listen, we'll see what happens with Lanterns Season 2. If, I think, the collective group of HBO and DC and Chris Mundy and the team all feel like we've got something that is a worthy successor to quite a beloved first season of television, then I wouldn't be surprised to see more."

While official news on the future of Lanterns remains up in the air, this report paints a grim picture for the future of the DCU which was, somewhat tragically, only just getting started.

items.title: Shaquille O'Neal is Starring in a Game Show Where Players Have to Hide Him in Plain Sight
items.description: In one of the more amusing sidequests that Shaquille O’Neal has undertaken in his life, the former NBA All-Star is set to appear in a game show where players try to conceal him from view in a hilarious twist on hide-and-seek.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
In one of the more amusing sidequests that Shaquille O’Neal has embarked on in his life, the former NBA All-Star is set to appear in a game show where players try to conceal him from view in a hilarious twist on hide-and-seek.

Can You Hide… Shaq? Is the name of this upcoming game show, which will premiere with two episodes at 9 PM on Thursday, December 3, on ABC and the ESPN app. Episodes will be available to stream on Hulu starting December 4.

The show pits two teams of contestants against each other, challenging them to hide Shaq in plain sight in public areas around Dallas, Texas. This is no small feat, given that Shaq is a massive former athlete and one of the world's most recognizable celebrities.

“I’m 7-foot-1. I’m not exactly easy to miss,” Shaquille O’Neal said, per Variety. “I love meeting people wherever I go, but for years I’ve always wondered, could somebody actually make me disappear? Well, we finally decided to put it to the test. We turned it into a real competition, and I can’t wait for you to see the creative, ridiculous ways they tried to hide me in plain sight. The stakes are high, and so is the prize. But you know me, we’re gonna have some fun along the way.”

Comedian Nicole Byer will host the program, which promises to be a competition full of “fast, funny, and unpredictable challenges.”

The show's logline lays out the rules: “Contestants first split into two teams, each with a set mission and time clock. The team that completes its mission with the fewest spottings earns immunity for one team member in the next round, who then becomes team captain. The teams must work together toward one greater mission: earning prize money to add to the ‘Shaq-pot’ that will ultimately be claimed by one winner.”

As of yet, the amount in the ‘Shaq-pot’ is unknown, but it had better be worth it, given how undoubtedly difficult it is to disguise one of the NBA’s most famous players. Can you hide… Shaq? Is produced by Jersey Legends Productions and Fulwell Entertainment in partnership with ESPN. Executive producers listed are Shaquille O’Neal, Colin Smeeton, Jeremy Castro, Charlie Van Vleet, Adam Cooper, Ben Winston, Mike Paris, and Emma Conway.

Shaq has undertaken no small amount of passion projects in his career; aside from his legacy as a sports legend, he's also a dubstep artist (under the name DJ Diesel), rapper, actor, and has even appeared in a few video games, including Fortnite and of course, Shaq Fu.

I personally can't wait to see how contestants manage to hide Shaq in this show. Let us know what your strategy would be in the comments, and whether or not you'll be watching come December 3.

items.title: Nintendo Opens New Job Role to Preserve and Organize its Old Games
items.description: Nintendo of America has opened up a new job position to help preserve and archive the older games in its vast library of titles.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Nintendo of America has opened up a new job position to help preserve and archive the older games in its vast library.

Nintendo has released around 11,000 games in its lifetime. Now, it’s looking to organize those games — at least, the older ones — with a specialized role at its Redmond, WA location.

As per the official job description, Nintendo of America’s future Digital Archivist, Historical Systems will support the “preservation, organization, and accessibility of historical hardware and software information” by designing and implementing a “structured framework for organizing technical records, engineering documentation, source materials, and institutional knowledge related to legacy systems and platforms.”

Essentially, the digital archivist is a librarian of sorts, whose job is to create a means of organizing and documenting all of Nintendo’s older games, systems, and platforms, as well as any documentation or materials related to them. It definitely sounds like a fun role for video game history buffs, especially if they like organizing data.

The job listing describes its ideal candidate as someone with “expertise in archives, metadata management, information architecture, and research” who will work “closely with subject matter experts across engineering, product development, legal, and business teams” to “establish standards and processes that ensure historical information remains discoverable, usable, and preserved for future generations.”

The position is a 12-month contract role with a salary of $35-$55 per hour. A Bachelor’s degree in library & information science, Archives, Museum Studies, Information Management, History, Technical Communication, or a related field is preferred, although equivalent professional experience may be considered.

This is a major step forward for video game preservation, something that activists and enthusiasts in the space have been calling for for some time now. For example, the Video Game History Foundation was founded in 2016 with the intent of preserving and teaching the history of video games. Since then, it has worked toward creating the United States’ first dedicated library for the study of video game history, as well as preserving games’ source code.

Given Nintendo’s relevance in the games industry and its role in the history of the medium, it makes sense that the company would seek to archive its works. Perhaps this could result in some unexpected discoveries; for example, one collector came across 97 copies of an unreleased version of Super Mario Bros. Duck Hunt earlier this year, five of which were graded perfect 10s by PSA.

items.title: DC's New Leader Will Reportedly Prioritize More Well-Known Characters Like Batman and Wonder Woman, Reboot Has Yet to Be Decided
items.description: DC Studios' new boss is reportedly planning to prioritize more mainstream characters like Batman and Wonder Woman going forward.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
DC Studios' new boss is reportedly planning to prioritize more mainstream characters like Batman and Wonder Woman going forward.

Earlier this week, it was announced that DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran were stepping down (reports indicate they were actually fired), and now... we have an idea of what the new direction for the franchise may look like.

According to a new report from The Wrap, DC Studios' new incoming CEO, Jeremy Latcham, is expected to focus only on the hits going forward. The report claims that Latcham has been tasked by Skydance CEO David Ellison to assemble the Justice League on the big screen as quickly as possible. That means prioritizing projects with The Flash, Wonder Woman, Batman, and other heroes that the average filmgoer would recognize.

As a result, don't expect bigger swings with more niche characters like Clayface, Booster Gold, or Peacemaker. The report even name-checked "modest" characters like Supergirl as not being a focus going forward.

As of right now, DC has yet to decide if they will need to wipe the slate clean again and do a full reboot, with new actors and storylines. The universe is still so young and has yet to interconnect with all of its installments, so there's room to pivot... and it would be a PR disaster to recast David Corenswet after also publicly dumping Henry Cavill just a few years ago.

The focus on mainstream characters is the direct inverse of James Gunn's style, as he really rose in prominence with Guardians of the Galaxy, a film about a group of misfits that the general audience wasn't very familiar with. Gunn tried to extend that to the DCU to mixed results. Many have been wondering where Gunn's Batman is, particularly after he was a no-show in Clayface. Gunn did open this universe with Superman, and a sequel is on the way, but it's not quite enough for fans.

The early slate of projects has led to frustrations among viewers that Gunn isn't building enough momentum to bring the biggest characters to the center of the DCU. Ironically, Gunn had recently stated that Superman, Wonder Woman, and Batman were going to be pivotal to the DCU, so it seems he was building to it, but seemingly not fast enough for Skydance.

The Wrap also noted that Latcham will refrain from having a big social media presence, as Gunn was known for being active to a fault. Although he would answer fan questions, he would also sometimes create confusion, get into feuds with fans, and it didn't always create the best image of DC. It's unclear what the next era of DC will look like, but hopefully it's not as chaotic and tumultuous as fans are expecting, since this franchise has been through enough already.

items.title: World of Warcraft Forever Hotfix Will Thin Out Overcrowded Zones and Help Faction Balance
items.description: World of Warcraft Forever has been incredibly popular, and has gone down as the biggest WoW launch in history. It's little wonder then, that some zones are absolutely packed with players. And, Blizzard has implemented a fix.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
World of Warcraft Forever has been incredibly popular, and has gone down as the biggest WoW launch in history. It's little wonder, then, that some zones are absolutely packed with players — but thankfully, Blizzard has implemented a fix.

In a hotfix last night, Blizzard lowered the population in overcrowded zones, which should give players more of a chance to get quests done without competing with a hundred other players to tag a spider. In the developers' notes, Blizzard also noted that "We’ve made this an even bigger change on the PvP ruleset, following feedback from players that they felt overcrowded in several places. We will continue to monitor how zones feel and make further adjustments as necessary."

Unlike past versions of WoW, which had a variety of servers available, World of Warcraft Forever has one server that's divided into different rulesets: PvP, PvE, RPPvP, RP and Hardcore. Instead of dividing players among different servers, Blizzard uses layering to group people into different instances of the world. And because WoW Forever's whole thing is being surrounded by other players, Blizzard seemingly opted to try and get as many people into each layer as possible without causing problems.

However, while it's fun to see hundreds of players running around each zone, this approach has caused some issues. Some people on the PvE rulesets have reported difficulties in being able to finish quests, especially in the earlier zones, as they have to compete with dozens of different players to get anything done. But the problem is especially bad for players in the PvP rulesets because of a faction imbalance.

At least here in the US, The Horde is much more popular than The Alliance, and that's causing problems. For Alliance players, they're outnumbered when they're questing in the world, which means they get killed instantly in later zones. For Horde players, they can't create new toons, because Blizzard is throttling character creation to try and preserve faction balance.

Blizzard Community Manager Kaivax has addressed this in a seperate note last night, saying, "It’s vitally important that the PvP rulesets in WoW: Forever have balanced factions where both factions vie for supremacy, creating memories of epic victories and stunning defeats that we all remember for years to come. While even the most extreme case in a region is currently at roughly a 55/45 split, that is not as close as we want it to be." Blizzard wants to get that balance as close to 50/50 as possible.

To address the matter, Kaivax says, "In the short term, that means that it will become increasingly difficult to create characters on the more populous faction in each region – currently Horde on North American PvP rulesets or Alliance in EU Roleplay-PvP. As everyone settles and shifts, these may flip to the other side."

Despite some of these growing pains, though, World of Warcraft Forever is still proving to be one of the smoothest launches in Blizzard history. Launch night went off without a hitch, thanks to the servers running on around 251TB of RAM and over 70,000 CPU cores.

November 9, 2026

Classes

  • Druid
    • The Cooldown Manager no longer shows Berserk, and now correctly shows Lacerate when learned.
    • Idol of Ferocity no longer lists Mangle as an ability it discounts.
    • Feral
      • Fixed an issue where Feral Charge (Cat) was not putting the Druid in combat right away.
      • Fixed an issue where Natural Instinct was not applying correctly to Lacerate or Pounce.
      • Fixed an issue where the Pounce Stun debuff was not showing in the enemy debuffs while active.
  • Hunter
    • Vulgara the Insatiable and the Shrieklings of Zephras should now belong to the correct hunter pet families.
    • Fixed an issue causing Hunters to sometimes aggro enemies from very far away by targeting them.

    • Flamestirke’s ticks on the ground no longer incorrectly consume clearcasting.

    • Fixed an issue that prevented the throne room doors from opening if the party wiped while fighting Emperor Thaurissan.

  • The Drowned City
    • Fixed an issue that was causing creatures inside the Drowned City to do about 30% more damage than intended.

    • The Shaper’s Terrace: Vitrix, Snowtalon, and Cinder now correctly drop loot and higher-level skinning materials.

    • Fixed an issue that allowed players to mount inside Stratholme.

  • Teldrassil - Spawn time reduced for Ferocitas the Dream Eater.
  • Un’goro Crater - Fixed an issue that was causing Young Diemetradons to spawn at level 58 (rather than 51 to 52).
  • Zephras - Malduko Cloudcrush now respawns slightly more slowly.

Items

  • Fixed an issue with the Pouch of Violet Dust preventing players from receiving an extra hour of duration of the Camp Benefits aura as intended.
  • Fixed a bug that prevented Waylaid Crates and Craftsman’s Writs from dropping inside dungeons.
  • Berdun’s Trusty Rifle no longer has random stats and is not Bind-on-Equip.
  • Fixed a bug causing Nifty Stopwatch to share a cooldown with Dash, Blink, Sprint, and other movement abilities.
  • Zephrali Greatstaff and Fallen Dragon’s Scepter now appear correctly oriented when sheathed on the player’s back.
  • Gloves of Holy Might now work as intended.

Player versus Player

  • Removed an invisible wall that was incorrectly blocking the roof of the Alliance base in Warsong Gulch. Please be careful up there.

Quests

  • “The Monster Surfaces” quest item is now available to all players in a party.
  • “Croaky’s Head” is now available to all players in a party.
  • “Elmpaw’s Head” is now available to all players in a party.
  • Mistreating Astor Hadren during the quest “The Deathstalkers” should now properly anger him, allowing you to fight him.
  • Fixed a bug preventing Jom-jom from continuing his escape on “Jom-jom’s Escape”.
  • The door available after the quest “Ever After” should now correctly teleport players who interact with the door.
  • Fixed a bug keeping Terry Longdrink alive during the quest “Unwelcome Guests”.
  • Fixed an issue where the quest “Find Bingles” was incorrectly categorized in Ironforge, rather than Loch Modan.
  • Updated Skonk’s list to be readable by everyone going on “A Quick Grocery Run”.
  • Henrig Lonebrow’s Journal now respawns more quickly, so that more players can get started on “Lonebrow’s Journal”. It has also moved slightly down the road. Look for a similar skeleton to mark the location.
  • Addressed an issue that could prevent players from looting Berard’s Journal from Berard’s Bookshelf for “A Recipe for Death”.
  • Resolved an issue preventing completion of “Fetch ‘n’ Fletch”.
  • Fixed an issue where restarting the Rogue quest “Mission: Possible not Probable” was much less possible than intended.
  • Resolved an issue where Jezap Jinglesprocket could fail to provide players a “Bloodmaster’s Ring”.
  • Fixed an issue during the quest “Feathers in Flight” where players below level 60 could not loot the Hyjal Owl Nests.

Races

    • Cultivation now correctly only goes on cooldown after completing the cast.

World

  • Lowered the population of players in various zones where there was significant congestion.
    • Developers’ notes: We’ve made this an even bigger change on the PvP ruleset, following feedback from players that they felt overcrowded in several places. We will continue to monitor how zones feel and make further adjustments as necessary.
  • Resolved an issue where the flight path from Camp Taurajo to Thunder Bluff could unintentionally go through objects.

items.title: PlayStation Cancels Live-Service Heist Shooter, Fairgames
items.description: Fairgames, a live-service heist game from PlayStation's Haven Studios, has been canceled by Sony.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Fairgames, a live-service heist game from PlayStation's Haven Studios, has been canceled by Sony.

A new report from Bloomberg reveals that Fairgames has been scrapped, three and a half years after its announcement. Developer Haven Studios will not be shut down, nor will there be any layoffs, as PlayStation has decided to turn the team into a support studio for other first-party projects. The decision to pull the plug on the game was made after a recent test did not meet internal expectations.

“While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” said executives Sean Decker and John Doyle in a note reviewed by Bloomberg. “Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.”

The test being referenced here is likely one that made some waves earlier this fall. A mysterious game known as Project Espresso, which looked a lot like Fairgames, began advertising private playtests with a gameplay trailer back in September. Not much is known about those tests, but they didn't seem to be very fruitful for the team.

Fairgames was announced in 2023 and has been the subject of scrutiny for some time. Some fans pushed back on PlayStation's live-service pivot during the early 2020s, as the company has always excelled with blockbuster single-player games. When Concord bombed, fans began to express even further revulsion toward titles like Fairgames. The project has also been soured by a number of setbacks, including departures of key developers and internal struggles.

Fairgames' cancelation marks yet another major failure for PlayStation's live-service efforts. Concord flopped, The Last of Us Online was scrapped, an online God of War game was killed, and Marathon has been struggling since launch. Helldivers 2, on the other hand, has been a big win for PlayStation. There's some hope that maybe Bungie's decision to revive Destiny 2 could be productive, but Sony seems to be moving away from live-service. The only other major live-service game from PlayStation on the horizon is 4:Loop, a new game from JJ Abrams' studio, Bad Robot. We'll see if it suffers a similar fate as these other titles.

items.title: Someone Got Halo 1 Running on a Sega Dreamcast
items.description: A developer has successfully gotten the original Halo: Combat Evolved, a day-one launch title for the original Xbox in 2001, ported and running on the Sega Dreamcast – in both campaign and multiplayer. And they've posted 28 minutes of gameplay footage from the campaign and multiplayer to prove it.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
A developer has successfully gotten the original Halo: Combat Evolved, a day-one launch title for the original Xbox in 2001, ported and running on the Sega Dreamcast – in both campaign and multiplayer. And he's posted 28 minutes of gameplay footage from the campaign and multiplayer to prove it.

X user and game developer "Jilted Valkyrie" uploaded the footage just days ahead of the 25th anniversary of both Halo and the Xbox itself. The Dreamcast, meanwhile, is a tad older, having launched in Japan in late 1998 and worldwide in late 1999. The footage shows a modified title screen displaying the title, "Halo: Dreamcast Evolved," with the legendary Halo theme music playing. It then shows multiplayer footage on a number of maps, including big ones like Sidewinder. Meanwhile, footage from the first mission of the campaign is there too. The framerate appears to dip below 30fps at times, but it doesn't take away from the technical marvel that is getting an Xbox game running on the older Dreamcast hardware.

Jilted Valkyrie says the campaign port is currently 77% complete, and he shouts out Dreamcast developer Falco Girgis for his help on the project. "If you like what you see, go give @falco_girgis a follow. Without his work in KOS and SH4ZAM, this unique, passionate port of Halo would not exist. He inspired me with his technical posts on GTA3 for Dreamcast to do something I always wondered about... Halo on Sega."

He later added, "It's not a 1:1 port, so the experience has completely new things to it not in any other version. There's even an entire new mode... plus who wouldn't want to play Halo online on Dreamcast?" He did not give details on the new mode, however. Finally, he says that he expects to release it this year.

As for modern Halo, Xbox seems set to reboot the franchise – or at the very least, the way Halo is made. Xbox leadership took development duties on the next mainline Halo away from Halo Studios (nee 343 Industries) and handed them to Activision, who will form a new team to helm the project. It's a bold move, and it remains to be seen if it can restore the series to its former glory.

items.title: PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for November 2026 Announced
items.description: November’s lineup of games on PlayStation Plus has been revealed by Sony.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
November’s lineup of games on PlayStation Plus has been revealed by Sony.

Ahead of the holiday season, PlayStation Plus members are getting a wide variety of free games that they can try out on the service, including two big titles from Kojima Productions and Ryu Ga Gotoku.

The first game on this list is Death Stranding 2: On the Beach. The sequel to the first Death Stranding game, this follow-up takes eleven months after the events of its predecessor, featuring Sam Porter Bridges and Fragile as they set out across Australia to connect surviving colonies with the Chiral Network. It’s well worth a play, especially with this deal on PS Plus; in our review, IGN’s Simon Cardy scored the game a 9 out of 10, calling it a “triumphant sequel that emphatically delivers on the promise of its original.”

Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii is the second game on this month’s list. Join an amnesiac Goro Majima after he wakes up stranded on an island, gather a crew of pirates, and uncover a hidden treasure in this spinoff of the Yakuza series. It’s a delightfully fun romp, and another title that’s well worth taking advantage of if you’re a PS Plus subscriber; IGN’s Tristan Ogilvie scored the game an 8 out of 10 in our review, calling it “a consistently captivating voyage that kept my timbers shivering whether on land or at sea.”

Other games included in this month’s PS Plus lineup are Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake, a reimagining of the beloved classic that earned a 9 out of 10 from our reviewer, as well as 2025 survival-action game Atomfall, first-person shooter Trepang2, and racing game MotoGP 26.

PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for November 2026

▪️Death Stranding 2

▪️Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii

▪️Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake

▪️Atomfall

▪️Trepang2

▪️MotoGP 26

▪️Hell Let Loose

▪️Cricket 26

PS+ Premium

▪️Freedom Wars Remastered

▪️Soul Reaver 2

Let us know which games you’re excited to try in the comments below! Although GTA 6 is likely going to take up the bulk of most players’ time, these titles might make for a good break between heists.

items.title: Burger King Italy Gets Official Magic: The Gathering Meal With Whopper-Themed Deck Boxes
items.description: Burger King just launched a Magic: The Gathering meal that comes with Whopper-themed deck boxes and sleeves. Unfortunately, the promotion is exclusive to Burger King Italy, with no indication that it will expand to other countries.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
Burger King just launched a Magic: The Gathering meal that comes with Whopper-themed deck boxes and sleeves. Unfortunately, the promotion is exclusive to Burger King Italy, with no indication that it will expand to other countries.

However, not all hope is lost for players from other regions — this is one of the first fast-food partnerships from Wizards of the Coast, following the trend of franchises like Pokémon. If the promotion goes well, it’s safe to expect more MTG collaborations across other regions in the future.

The Great Gathering Bundle (they use English on the official Burger King Italy site) includes your choice of a Chicken Krispper, Double Cheeseburger, or the plant-based Impossible Whopper with fries and a drink. It’s priced at €19.90, equivalent to roughly $22 USD, and is available now through November 30.

That sounds yummy and all, but the real kicker that’s both intrigued and frustrated Magic fans is the new TCG accessories. Each meal comes with a Burger King-themed deck box and 100 card sleeves, perfect for your silliest Commander deck. Both accessories, which can be see in the image above, are designed in the style of a Whopper burger, with an orange ‘sesame bun’ pattern, a patty, and layers of toppings.

Sturdy deck boxes on their own are rarely under $20, making the accessories a genuinely good deal. As it stands, however, the only way to get your hands on them is by going to Italy to chow down on some Burger King.

Unlike the Pokémon Happy Meal, the MTG Burger King collaboration does not include any promotional cards. This could be a good thing, as region-locked cards can compound ongoing scalping concerns in an already tumultuous TCG market. Still, I wouldn’t be surprised if the Burger King deck boxes end up becoming a hot commodity on EBay.

Keen customers have already been sharing their spoils online, picking up some buzz from online MTG communities and the ire of fans from other countries. One X user who got their hands on the collab praises the quality of the deck box, but suggests the sleeves "feel a little flimsy and cheap."

items.title: IGN to Stream the 2027 New York Game Awards
items.description: The 2027 New York Game Awards are on the horizon, and IGN will once again be the official destination to stream the broadcast.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The 2027 New York Game Awards are on the horizon, and IGN will once again be the official destination to stream the broadcast.

The 16th annual New York Game Awards will take place on November 19, 2026, where legendary voice actor Troy Baker (The Last of Us, Indiana Jones and the Great Circle) will be recognized as the Andrew Yoon Legend Award recipient.

In honor of the late Andrew Yoon, a member and journalist in the New York Videogame Critics Circle, this award honors “game changers” in the industry who have “propelled the gaming world forward, celebrating their profound impact on an industry that continues to captivate and connect people worldwide.”

“When we consider our upcoming Andrew Yoon Legend winners, we’re looking for individuals who’ve made a deep cultural impact on the video game landscape, and Troy Baker felt like the perfect addition,” Harold Goldberg, co-founder and president, NYVGCC, said in a statement. “Troy is such a force of nature within the games industry. We’ve recognized his voice-acting performances at previous New York Game Awards, and we are ecstatic to have him join our roster of Andrew Yoon Legend winners. Plus, our audiences are in for a treat with his musical performance after this year's awards. You’ll only get to experience that moment in person at SVA Theatre!”

“It’s hard to find a video game from the past 10 or 20 years without mentioning Troy Baker,” Reggie Fils-Aimé, the former president of Nintendo of America and NYVGCC board member, added. “It’s because his performances are so ingrained in some of the most beloved video games in recent history, and he brought personality and meaning to those characters.”

“Troy is someone who has left a mark on our students, both through his work and during his time speaking with them ahead of the awards,” said Ryan O’Callaghan, executive director for NYVGCC. “We couldn’t ask for a better legend winner to celebrate our 16th annual New York Game Awards.”

After the awards, Troy Baker will perform a concert for in-person attendees, which all ticket holders are eligible to attend. Tickets are priced at $85 and can be purchased through Humanitix, with a limited number of VIP tickets available for $100. VIP tickets grant purchasers preferred seating during the awards, as well as access to the official after-party presented by New Blood Interactive.

As previously mentioned, the awards will be livestreamed on IGN’s website and YouTube channels, as well as the New York Videogame Critics Circle’s official social media channels.

Proceeds from this year’s New York Game Awards will benefit the NYVGCC’s Playing with Purpose writing program, which brings journalism classes and workshops, as well as courses in game narrative writing, to schools and shelters throughout New York City. Playing with Purpose received its first National Endowment for the Arts grant this year, which will help expand its classes to students in the Hudson Valley Middletown School District, as well as its work at the Lab School for Finance and Technology, and High School for Fashion Industries.

items.title: PlayStation Plus PC App Will Go Offline December 10, as Sony Continues to Retreat From PC
items.description: Outside of the few games that Sony has ported to Windows, the PlayStation Plus app on PC was the best way to play PS5 games on PC, even if you had to stream them. But now, Sony will be retiring the PlayStation Plus PC app.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Outside of the few games that Sony has ported to Windows, the PlayStation Plus app on PC was the best way to play PS5 games on PC, even if you had to stream them. But now, Sony will be retiring the PlayStation Plus PC app.

In a blog post today, Sony announced that the PlayStation Plus app is going away on December 10 in order to focus on console users. Sony justified the decision by saying, "With a very small number of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members (less than 0.4%) using the PlayStation Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use. As a result, the PlayStation Plus cloud streaming app on PC will no longer be available."

This comes just a few months after Sony backed out of releasing PC ports of PlayStation exclusives, instead opting to keep its single-player games exclusive to its own consoles. Even the reasoning is similar, with Sony Interactive Entertainment CEO Herman Hulst telling employees that Sony's PC ports were 'inconsistent' and didn't make enough money.

However, with the PlayStation Plus app on PC going away, it's going to be a bit harder to stream games when you're away from your console, something you can easily do from your phone or PC with an Xbox Game Pass subscription – unless it's GTA 6, of course. With this change, the only streaming option for PS5 outside of a console is Remote Play, and that requires a console to be on the same network.

It's also worth mentioning that consoles are only getting more expensive, and the PS5 Pro will still set you back $1,559 at the time of writing on Amazon. As hardware gets more expensive, cloud streaming is going to be increasingly more important, and it seems like Sony is backing away from it – if even just a little bit.

Sony has avoided putting the same limitations on cloud gaming that other companies have, though. Just this month, Microsoft implemented a time limit on Xbox Cloud Streaming, limiting Game Pass Ultimate subscribers to just 15 hours of play time before they need to break out their wallets to buy extra time. Nvidia's GeForce Now also has time limits, but they're a bit more liberal, allowing 100 hours of playtime each month.

items.title: Logitech Is Letting Employees Take Work Off for Game Releases, Just Ahead of GTA 6
items.description: Logitech has announced that it will be giving employees the option to take time off for video game releases ahead of GTA 6's launch.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Logitech has announced that it will be giving employees the option to take time off for video game releases ahead of GTA 6's launch.

The tech company announced that it will label this perk as "Logi Game Day" for its employees. Logitech explained that this idea came about from an internal study, which concluded that "81% of gamers believe that gaming builds real-world confidence, reduces anxiety, and correlates with stronger day-to-day work performance." Another study noted that 98.8% of enterprise ITDM respondents believe that gaming translates to actual workplace skills, such as problem-solving and acting under pressure.

As a result, the company is going to lean into that and give people the freedom to take time off to play new video games.

“It’s time to retire the stereotype that gaming is a waste of time,” said Hanneke Faber, Logitech’s chief executive officer. “As a company designing products for work and play, we see every day how engagement in one sphere supports performance in the other.”

On November 19, Logitech G, the company's gaming division, will host a live-streamed event at its San Jose headquarters to celebrate the occasion. This, likely coincidentally, aligns with the release day of GTA 6. It's unclear exactly what the event will feature, but it will be hosted by Logitech G’s general manager, Robin Piispannen.

“Whether diving into a game like GTA 6 or Call of Duty Modern Warfare 4, shaving seconds off lap times in Forza, or teaming up in an online battle, Game Day gives our team a shared purpose," he says. “We see firsthand how Logitech employees who sharpen their skills in-game translate directly back to work & problem solving.”

GTA 6 is officially almost a week away from launch, and fans can officially preload the massive game starting today. Millions of people are expected to take the game's launch day off, and some countries are even advertising ways for people to do so. It's expected to be one of the biggest cultural events of the decade, if not the century. Rockstar hasn't revealed GTA 6's preorder data so far, but its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, has confirmed that they're "far in excess" of their expectations.

items.title: Bungie Tempts New Players With Free Period as PvE Mode and PvP Arena Battles Come to Marathon
items.description: PvE is coming to Marathon and Bungie is hoping new players will give it a shot with a free-to-play period at the start of the next Season. It’s called Symbiosis and is landing on December 8.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
PvE is coming to Marathon and Bungie is hoping new players will give it a shot with a free-to-play period at the start of the next Season. It’s called Symbiosis and is landing on December 8.

One of the big new changes is an update to Perimeter, giving the early game region a much-needed shake up. Previously, there was no in-between on the map, with matches either a constant meat grinder against other players or completely dead.

The zone update sees the playable zone expanded as alien trees sprout from the landscape. Now there are dark caves leading to a new POI called Reservoir, which features a large main room and catwalks for nasty ambushes. Oh, and there’s a giant crab boss now.

If you bounced off Marathon because of those aforementioned ambushes, Bungie is introducing a new mode just for you: PvE Expeditions. These let you test yourself against the tougher challenges Marathon has to offer (like big crabs) without the added threat of a team murdering you and stealing your stuff as soon as you pull it off.

Rather than taking the Arc Raiders approach and letting players play the normal extraction loop without the threat of other players, it’s seemingly a standalone mode Bungie is calling a “co-op PvE roguelite.” That means metaprogression, in-match upgrades, no two matches the same. From Bungie, it should be good stuff.

The upgrades in the new mode are called Flash Boosts and should let you become a god in an entirely new way each run. Challenges escalate with each layer you break through and scale with your power. Check out the trailer:

Bungie also introduces a new social space for Symbiosis. It’s called Limbo, and it’ll let you hang with your friends and test out kits.

It should be a good place to train with Bishop, the game’s new high-jumping and sword-slashing new Runner Shell. The trailer shows Bishop cutting through a whole gang of bots with his Ultimate.

On top of all this, there are new weapons and gadgets, as well as a new PvP deathmatch mode for people who want to get better at not being murdered in the normal extraction loop. Marathon will be free December 8-15, giving new players a chance to check it out when Symbiosis lands.

items.title: GTA 6 Fans Are Divided Over Confirmation of 30fps
items.description: GTA 6 will be 30fps, creating division among fans and frustration for PS5 Pro owners.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
GTA 6 will be 30fps, creating division among fans and frustration for PS5 Pro owners.

Rockstar Games confirmed today that GTA 6 will target 30fps on all consoles, including PS5 Pro. This answers one of the biggest questions that has surrounded the game for years, but the answer also likely isn't a big surprise to many. Given the scope and scale of this game, as well as Rockstar's history with other games, a lot of people assumed this would be a 30fps game. However, there was hope that PS5 Pro would offer 60fps, or at least a 40fps mode as a compromise.

Still, the confirmation is creating all kinds of waves across social media. Some fans are pretty understanding, noting that the trade-off for a lower frame rate is an extremely dense, visually intense game.

"It's a shame they could not get it running at 40-60fps, and it would’ve been way better to play at 60fps, but I also fully understand why this happened," said one fan. "You don’t get to make the most dense, detailed, and graphically intensive game of the generation without making sacrifices."

"GTA 6 has a ton of complex systems running at once and reaching that level of realism while maintaining a stable framerate is impossible due to the CPU bottleneck," explained another fan. "Rockstar Games probably had to choose between cutting down complex systems like NPC density, NPC AI, Cars, Random Events etc. for a higher framerate or keeping those while targeting 30FPS to reach the highest level of realism possible and now we know that they went with the latter."

"30fps in [Red Dead Redemption 2] is good enough," stated a user on X. "As long as input latency is lower and there are no significant frame drops, I think GTA 6 will be alright."

Others are not as generous, however. One fan refunded the Ultimate Edition of GTA 6, noting they'll wait for the inevitable PS6 version that will likely have performance enhancements, possibly including 60fps. A big part of the frustration comes from people who expected more out of the PS5 Pro. Some fans shelled out a lot of extra money for the console, assuming it would give them a notable leap in quality from the base console. While it will have some exclusive features, like ray-traced shadows and PSSR, it's not the jump that some were hoping for.

"People paid over a grand for slightly better upscaling + ray-tracing but still the same 30 fps performance," said a user on X.

"I understand that the game is massive, and that this was (probably) the only way it would’ve even been playable on a console, but damn," said another fan. "It’s 2026. 30fps?! I’m losing excitement for GTA 6 by the day."

"60fps is the floor for modern titles on PS5 Pro and above, not 30...but Rockstar are dragging us back a good 5-10 years here," said an annoyed fan on Reddit. "They knew the hardware capabilities, and chose to make a game that isn't really compatible with it...that's what's crazy here."

Another fan pointed out there may also be some hypocrisy regarding this situation, as games like Starfield have been panned for being 30fps: "No offense towards GTA 6 it will be good, but Starfield got assaulted for being locked to 30fps and runs at 60fps on Xbox and PS5 now, are we gonna have the same energy for GTA 6 being locked to 30fps?"

Many games offer some kind of performance mode to unlock higher frame rates, at the cost of a lower resolution, a lack of ray-tracing, or other compromises. However, it doesn't seem like GTA 6 will have that, much to the annoyance of some fans. Maybe there's a chance Rockstar will add some performance buffs post-launch, but I wouldn't hold my breath. Red Dead Redemption 2 has been stuck at 30fps on consoles since 2018.

There are rumors that a GTA 6 PC port will arrive in early 2027, which would likely be the definitive version of the game with much higher frame rates. Rockstar has yet to confirm any platforms for the game beyond Xbox and PlayStation (though you can play the game on Xbox One through the cloud), but maybe we'll hear more about a potential PC version in the new year.

Despite some division over performance options, GTA 6 is just nine days away from launch, and the hype is at its peak. Players can pre-load the game starting today, which they absolutely should if they want to play it as soon as it is available. The game will take up nearly 212 GBs, so it may take a while to download, depending on internet speeds. PlayStation and Xbox have also both confirmed that the game is the most pre-ordered title in their respective histories, meaning this game is likely going to shatter all kinds of sales records next week.

GTA 6 will be 30fps, creating division among fans and frustration for PS5 Pro owners.

Rockstar Games confirmed today that GTA 6 will target 30fps on all consoles, including PS5 Pro. This answers one of the biggest questions that has surrounded the game for years, but the answer also likely isn't a big surprise to many. Given the scope and scale of this game, as well as Rockstar's history with other games, a lot of people assumed this would be a 30fps game. However, there was hope that PS5 Pro would offer 60fps, or at least a 40fps mode as a compromise.

Still, the confirmation is creating all kinds of waves across social media. Some fans are pretty understanding, noting that the trade-off for a lower frame rate is an extremely dense, visually intense game.

"It's a shame they could not get it running at 40-60fps, and it would’ve been way better to play at 60fps, but I also fully understand why this happened," said one fan. "You don’t get to make the most dense, detailed, and graphically intensive game of the generation without making sacrifices."

"GTA 6 has a ton of complex systems running at once and reaching that level of realism while maintaining a stable framerate is impossible due to the CPU bottleneck," explained another fan. "Rockstar Games probably had to choose between cutting down complex systems like NPC density, NPC AI, Cars, Random Events etc. for a higher framerate or keeping those while targeting 30FPS to reach the highest level of realism possible and now we know that they went with the latter."

"30fps in [Red Dead Redemption 2] is good enough," stated a user on X. "As long as input latency is lower and there are no significant frame drops, I think GTA 6 will be alright."

Others are not as generous, however. One fan refunded the Ultimate Edition of GTA 6, noting they'll wait for the inevitable PS6 version that will likely have performance enhancements, possibly including 60fps. A big part of the frustration comes from people who expected more out of the PS5 Pro. Some fans shelled out a lot of extra money for the console, assuming it would give them a notable leap in quality from the base console. While it will have some exclusive features, like ray-traced shadows and PSSR, it's not the jump that some were hoping for.

"People paid over a grand for slightly better upscaling + ray-tracing but still the same 30 fps performance," said a user on X.

"I understand that the game is massive, and that this was (probably) the only way it would’ve even been playable on a console, but damn," said another fan. "It’s 2026. 30fps?! I’m losing excitement for GTA 6 by the day."

"60fps is the floor for modern titles on PS5 Pro and above, not 30...but Rockstar are dragging us back a good 5-10 years here," said an annoyed fan on Reddit. "They knew the hardware capabilities, and chose to make a game that isn't really compatible with it...that's what's crazy here."

Another fan pointed out there may also be some hypocrisy regarding this situation, as games like Starfield have been panned for being 30fps: "No offense towards GTA 6 it will be good, but Starfield got assaulted for being locked to 30fps and runs at 60fps on Xbox and PS5 now, are we gonna have the same energy for GTA 6 being locked to 30fps?"

Many games offer some kind of performance mode to unlock higher frame rates, at the cost of a lower resolution, a lack of ray-tracing, or other compromises. However, it doesn't seem like GTA 6 will have that, much to the annoyance of some fans. Maybe there's a chance Rockstar will add some performance buffs post-launch, but I wouldn't hold my breath. Red Dead Redemption 2 has been stuck at 30fps on consoles since 2018.

There are rumors that a GTA 6 PC port will arrive in early 2027, which would likely be the definitive version of the game with much higher frame rates. Rockstar has yet to confirm any platforms for the game beyond Xbox and PlayStation (though you can play the game on Xbox One through the cloud), but maybe we'll hear more about a potential PC version in the new year.

Despite some division over performance options, GTA 6 is just nine days away from launch, and the hype is at its peak. Players can pre-load the game starting today, which they absolutely should if they want to play it as soon as it is available. The game will take up nearly 212 GBs, so it may take a while to download, depending on internet speeds. PlayStation and Xbox have also both confirmed that the game is the most pre-ordered title in their respective histories, meaning this game is likely going to shatter all kinds of sales records next week.
